subject: Re: Budget range validation — monthly token spend and procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Budget range validation — post-call follow-up

Hey Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks for the call earlier today — helpful overview of Redwood and the Dedicated options. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance:

1) We want to validate monthly spend bands for planning. Rough expected volume: 200M–800M tokens/month initially, with potential to hit ~2B in 6–9 months if model usage ramps.
2) We have a procurement threshold where anything above ~$50k/month needs VP-level approval and a 3–6 week procurement cycle. Anything above ~$200k/month requires legal review and a longer SLA negotiation.
3) Can you share indicative $/1M token ranges you see for dedicated vs hosted (and how quantization / batching might change that)? Also any recommended banding (e.g., 0–50M, 50–250M, 250–1M, 1M+) with typical unit economics would be great.

Attached a simple spend model we use — acme_pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet). Happy to jump on a quick call if needed.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Product
Acme Financial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation — post-call follow-up

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the model. Quick recap and a few clarifying Qs so we can give realistic bands:

Recap from our end:
- Your current expected steady-state is ~200M–800M tokens/month; potential to scale to ~2B/month within 6–9 months.
- Procurement thresholds: >$50k/mo (VP approval), >$200k/mo (legal + SLA).

High-level Redwood guidance (indicative; final pricing depends on commit, model, latency SLOs):
- Hosted API (managed): approximately $7–$25 per 1M tokens depending on model family and concurrency. Best for proof-of-concept and low-latency small volumes.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity): typically $2–$12 per 1M tokens depending on commit size, quantization (INT8/4) and batching. With aggressive quantization and large commits you can approach the low end.

Suggested monthly spend bands (ballpark ranges):
- Band A: 0–50M tokens -> $350–$1,250/month (hosted pricing typical)
- Band B: 50M–250M tokens -> $350–$6,250/month (mix of hosted + small dedicated)
- Band C: 250M–1B tokens -> $500–$12,000/month (dedicated recommended; unit $/1M in the $2–$12 range)
- Band D: 1B+ tokens -> $2,000–$24,000+/month (volume pricing, tighter commits, multi-GPU pools)

Notes / assumptions:
- These are example ranges to help with procurement bands. Actuals vary by model (decoder-only vs chat-optimized), avg tokens per request, and whether you enable KV/prefix caching.
- We assume a mix of generation and embeddings; embeddings have different unit economics. If you can share a rough split (generation vs embeddings) and avg prompt+completion length we can tighten these numbers.

Questions for you:
- Do the token bands above align with procurement skew (e.g., does finance want a single monthly number or low/high scenario)?
- Can you confirm expected embeddings % vs generation % and avg tokens per call?
- Is Acme able to consider a 6–12 month reserved commit if we gave a lower $/1M at commit tiers? That often helps keep spend below those VP/legal thresholds.

Next steps: Rafael and I will prepare a short 1-pager showing committed vs on-demand cost scenarios and a recommended commit level to stay under the $50k/month threshold if that's a hard constraint. Rafael — we'll loop Dev for rough perf/latency assumptions.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Budget range validation — post-call follow-up

Alex / Marissa — attaching a quick pricing tiers PDF that breaks out unit economics and the impact of commits/quantization. Key callouts:

- Example unit economics (decoder-generation workload, avg 150 tokens per transaction):
  • No commit (hosted): ~$12–$20 / 1M tokens
  • Small commit (50k USD/mo equivalent): ~$6–$10 / 1M tokens
  • Mid commit (200k USD/mo): ~$2.5–$6 / 1M tokens

- With INT8 quantization and 4-bit kernels for compatible models we typically see 20–40% token cost reductions on dedicated capacity.
- Batching and caching (prefix reuse) can further reduce billed tokens by ~10–30% depending on workload.

If the primary ask is to stay under $50k/month to avoid VP procurement, rough guidance:
- Aim for a commit in the $40k–$60k/month band (gives you predictable unit economics and simplifies procurement).
- If you can commit to 6–12 months we can lower the mid-commit price band near $2.5–$4 / 1M tokens.

Attaching: redwood_pricing_tiers_v2.pdf (pricing tiers summary).

We can run a quick calc with your acme_pricing_model.xlsx if you drop it back to us with the gen vs embed split and avg tokens per call. Dev — can you confirm whether our INT8 quant path supports the model family Alex mentioned (sm-core-1)?

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.ai>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget range validation — post-call follow-up

Thanks — that is super helpful and close to what our procurement team expects. Quick answers:

- Procurement wants a single planning number for the SOW sign-off. We typically provide a low/expected/high scenario. For now we can use:
  • Low: 150M tokens/mo (~$9k–$22k)
  • Expected: 500M tokens/mo (~$15k–$60k)
  • High: 2B tokens/mo (~$30k–$240k)

- Gen vs embed split: roughly 80% generation, 20% embeddings. Avg tokens per gen call ~180 (prompt+completion).
- Procurement note: to avoid the VP-level approval step we'd like to keep initial monthly spend forecast under $50k. If committing to a 6 month reserved commit at ~$40k/mo equivalent is an option, that will make the green light much more likely.

Next step: I'll share this with Finance and Procurement and loop Samantha Lee (procurement lead) if things look good. Could you both send the 1-pager and the committed vs on-demand calc by EOD Friday?

Appreciate it — Alex
